issues.claim: §4.11 *The clock* (3) (l. 7713) gives the week of the year as '`(week mod 52) + 1`', but under history-first generation the replayed past lies at negative weeks (a standalone map's creation week is 0 and the replay epochs precede it; V06 §3.20.3), and `mod` of a negative integer is left undefined (a truncating remainder yields 0 … −51, so `+ 1` gives weeks ≤ 0 that no `CalendarRow` season holds). The season read by the Works' pauses and §8.2's season rows is then undefined for every replayed epoch; V06's cross-part note (e) asks for a floored modulo and it was not applied.
issues.required_change: In *The clock* (3) read: '`CalendarRow` gives the week of the year, `floorMod(week, 52) + 1` (the floored modulo, so a negative week of the replayed past maps into 1…52; V06 §3.20.3)'; add the case to EP-15 (history-first generation) with its B-EDGE fixture (a replay starting 300 years before a week-0 creation reads a valid season at every epoch).

issues.claim: `WaterBody.spring.flow` has a written reader that the pipeline does not implement. The model (§2.3, l. 986: read by 'the water pull on the growth field (§4.2 S3, §4.4), the prosperity field's water term (§4.5), wells …' — 'the pull weighted by `spring.flow`; volume 6's failing spring lowers `flow` over epochs'), V06 §3.12.1 (flow's only writer) and the rewrite-model/-V06 cross-part notes make S3 (6)'s `q(x)` and §4.5's water term weight a spring or oasis by `flow`; S3 (6) (l. 4927–4934) defines `q(x)` as '1 on a river bank, a lake or oasis shore, a spring or ground of the top well-yield class' with no `flow`, and §4.5's water term (l. 5552–5553) only says 'a spring or oasis that fails weakens its pull (V06)' without the mechanism. So item 111 (b)'s weakening pull has no defined rule in the base and `flow` is an orphan field on the pipeline side.
issues.required_change: In §4.2 S3 (6) define `q(x)` for a spring or an oasis shore as `flow × (1 − d ÷ pullRadius)` — `flow` the body's `spring.flow` (§2.3; 1 when made, lowered by V06 §3.12.1) — and read the same `q(x)` in §4.5's water term; state in §4.5 'a failing spring weakens its pull through `spring.flow` (§2.3; V06 §3.12.1)'; add EP-14's companion case (a spring at `flow` 0 pulls nothing, its oasis kept as a lake) to §4.13.
